description: Every field the query tools accept, each with its meaning, unit, whether it can be missing, and which bars (1d, 1h) it exists on. Open — no key needed. Call this before query_cross_section, screen_universe or query_series. Percentile, z-score and the top_pct/bottom_pct conditions rank within the markets your plan can see, so they need a wide slice.
name: list_fields

FieldDoc.description:
One addressable field's documentation.

Served verbatim by the MCP plane's `list_fields`; the schema derive is what
keeps the tool's advertised output shape and the served JSON the same thing.

best_horizon_hours.description: Horizon (hours) at which the field's signal is strongest/most durable.

class.description:
Which signal class the field belongs to, when it has been measured:
`state` (durable, 24 h horizon, retention ≈ 1), `microstructure`
(same-bar, decays under the entry delay), `momentum` (short-term
reversal that survives the delay) or `no_signal`. Absent for stored
columns that were never measured on their own.

delay_retention.description:
Share of `ic_fwd` left when entry is delayed by the source's real
publication lag (~2 h). Near 1 means durable; near 0 means same-bar only.

grains.description: Plane grains on which this field is available, in canonical order.

horizon_hours.description:
Horizon (hours) at which `ic_fwd`, `ic_back` and `delay_retention` are
stated.

ic_back.description:
Backward-placebo IC at `horizon_hours`: large values mean the forward IC
is partly contemporaneous with the return, not predictive of it.

kind.description:
`stored` (a column in the plane's own source) or `factor` (computed at
query time over a trailing window, or from the selected end row).

meaning.description: Plain-English meaning, authored in the semantic layer.

nullable.description: Whether the value can be absent for a market on a selected interval.

type.description:
The stored column's type (`float64`, `uint32`, `date32`, …); absent for
query-time factors, which are always floats.

unit.description:
The unit the values actually carry (`usd_notional`, `base_units`,
`ratio`, `fraction`, `count`, `date`, …). A stored column name is never a
synonym for its unit — the OI a caller sees is USD notional where the
column is named for the notion.

fields.description: Every field the query tools accept.
